explanations.2: This creates a file path by taking the original file path and adding '.eli5.json' to the end, so if the file was 'example.js', this would be 'example.js.eli5.json'.
explanations.6: JSON.parse converts a string of JSON text into a JavaScript object so we can actually use the data inside it.
explanations.7: This checks two things: that eli5Data has a property called 'explanations', AND that explanations is an object (not null or an array).
explanations.11: JSON.stringify does the opposite of parse — it converts our JavaScript object back into a string of JSON so it can be stored as an attribute value.
